paragraphs: Compare the actual work in airframes, powerplants and avionics. Check organization scope, supervision and assigned authority. The jurisdiction and duties determine whether to check an individual license, release qualifications or aircraft type. Then check tools, documents and shifts.

The comparison is based on O*NET 49-3011.00, the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook and public material on the relevant adjacent occupations; the adjacent-occupation part serves only to explain the boundary and does not mean that licences, type ratings or employment requirements can be transferred between them.

The table below compares the three directions within this occupation and three adjacent occupations on the same dimensions: the direction, the core work and output, the key difference, and what choice suits whom.
Focused on structures and mechanical systems; it involves cleaning, sealing, riveting and composite repair, and makes heavy demands on physical effort and tools.
People willing to do structural repair and to accept physical effort and a noisy environment.
Inspect and repair the fuselage, wings, tail, landing gear and hydraulic systems, carrying out structural repair, skin replacement and non-destructive testing.
Airframe maintenance direction (airframe)
Focused on engines and accessories; it involves special tools, rigging and engine run-ups, with high precision and safety requirements.
People willing to do engine removal, installation and fault diagnosis.
Remove, install and overhaul engines and accessories, test the running condition and troubleshoot, and adjust and replace parts to the manual.
Powerplant maintenance direction (powerplant)
Focused on electronic systems and wiring; troubleshooting relies on wiring diagrams, test equipment and version records, and the environment is relatively clean but demands care.
People who would rather test and troubleshoot electronic systems.
Install, test, adjust and repair electronic systems such as communication, navigation, flight instruments and automatic flight.
Avionics direction (49-2091)
Carries design and certification responsibility; maintenance technicians carry out maintenance and inspection to the manual.
People willing to do design and analysis, who usually need an engineering education.
Design aircraft and systems, set out the airworthiness certification plan and analyse performance and structures.
Aerospace engineers (adjacent occupation)
The object is industrial equipment rather than aircraft; it does not involve airworthiness documents or release responsibility.
People who would rather maintain industrial equipment.
Install, maintain and repair plant equipment and mechanical systems.
Industrial machinery mechanics (adjacent occupation)
Focused on compliance and oversight; maintenance technicians are focused on carrying out maintenance and releasing within the authority granted.
People who would rather do compliance checking and oversight.
Inspect aircraft and maintenance organisations against the regulations and verify airworthiness and compliance status.
Aviation inspectors (adjacent occupation)
Check local rules and organization authorization for the task. Verify independent work, inspection and return-to-service signing separately.
AI tools and review responsibilities

May 2025 OEWS covers U.S. wage and salary workers. The self-employed are outside the survey scope. Each SOC is a separate group. There is no combined estimate in this comparison.
